A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdamW scaling study. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original ResNet-18 and ViT experiments on CIFAR-10 and downsampled ImageNet, NanoGPT experiments on OpenWebText, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds the dataset-size learning-rate transfer results in Figure 12.

M1.justification: The AdamW procedure, scale-invariant network modifications, and proposed dataset-size and model-width scaling rules are retained. The added derivation and discussion do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10, downsampled ImageNet, and OpenWebText coverage is unchanged. New Figure 12 uses existing ImageNet classification coverage; billion-parameter and single-epoch findings are attributed to other work.

E2.justification: Figure 12 adds an explicit fixed-decay control to the dataset-size learning-rate transfer comparison: λ = 0.1 versus λ = 0.1 × 128,000/N. The existing fixed-decay comparisons for model-width transfer remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds learning-rate sweeps across four ImageNet subset sizes, from 160,000 to 1,280,000 samples, using 100 epochs and a fixed batch size under fixed versus inversely scaled decay. This supplements the earlier fixed-learning-rate decay sweeps; retained experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 12 tests whether the decrease in optimal learning rate with dataset size persists after inverse-N decay scaling. Existing normalization and initialization ablations, weight-norm analysis, and learning-rate schedule checks are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging image-classification results over three random seeds and using one seed for LLM pretraining. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds ResNet and ViT training/test accuracy and loss curves. These show optimal learning rates decreasing with dataset size at fixed decay and becoming more stable with inverse-N decay scaling. The earlier reported results and plotted curves are retained.

T1.justification: New Appendix C defines scalar relative update size and derives r = sqrt(2γ) for a steady-state EMA with independent, identically distributed zero-mean inputs. This adds a bounded theoretical connection; Theorem 1 and the earlier proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution bullets now explicitly condition inverse-dataset-size decay scaling on a fixed learning-rate schedule and width scaling on μP learning-rate scaling. These qualify the summary statements while retaining the same central contributions, abstract, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 materially expands applicability qualifications. Section 3.1 discusses correlated AdamW updates, while Section 5.1 distinguishes the paper's fixed-batch, repeated-data experiments from batch-size scaling and single-epoch pretraining. The cited single-epoch, token-per-parameter-dependent timescale law identifies an important boundary to the central constant-timescale prescription.

D1.justification: Figure 12 supplies the added experiment's decay values, normalization factor, training duration, and rationale for choosing decay near 0.1. Existing model specifications, implementation instructions, hardware disclosures, code links, and hyperparameter grids are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bergsma et al. (2025a), Dey et al. (2025), Narayan et al. (2025), and Schaipp et al. (2025), expanding discussion of subsequent scaling research and clarifying connections to Wortsman and Kosson. The anonymous Straight to Zero reference becomes Bergsma et al. (2025b), representing the same work.

P1.justification: Related work is divided into Work after us and Work before us, explanatory passages and an Impact Statement are added, and several wording and cross-reference errors are corrected. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the multipanel Figure 12 with its legend and caption. Earlier Figures 12–18 become Figures 13–19 without changes to their plotted content; the remaining visual changes mainly involve text reflow and updated captions or numbering.

improvement.justification: Figure 12 supplies a direct learning-rate transfer check absent from v2, Appendix C adds a useful formal connection, and the expanded discussion better identifies limits of the scaling rule. These strengthen support and interpretation without changing the main method or experimental breadth. The new derivation remains restricted to independent inputs, and broader LLM findings remain attributed to other work.
